title: Undead Warluck Lunar Luck Curse Concept
summary: Concept frame for an undead warluck whose perception-heavy, intelligence-weighted luck magic is tied to lunar phases and punishes attempts to steal or manipulate their fortune as a slow, escalating misfortune effect.
purpose: Provide a structured concept specification for the undead warluck archetype so it can be plugged into systems, backstories, and mechanics later without losing core identity: lunar luck, curse reflection, and investigation-grade perception.

coredefinition.identity: An undead caster-class archetype (warluck) who manipulates probability rather than raw elements.
coredefinition.lucknature: Luck is treated as a manipulable but reactive field: attempts to steal it rebound as accruing misfortune over time.
coredefinition.undeadanchor: Death decoupled the warluck from ordinary fate; they now act as a fixed reference point that luck rebounds around instead of through.
coredefinition.moonbinding: The character’s effective luck profile waxes and wanes with lunar phase, shifting between personal fortune, curse strength, and fortune-stripping.
coredefinition.perceptionbias: High perception and intelligence bias the warluck toward reading patterns, tells, and anomalies before acting, aligning with DARAD-style investigation.

identityframe.label: Undead Warluck Identity

attributes.perceptionstyle: Holmesian observer using DARAD and W5 to stabilize perception before action

identityframe.onelinetranslation: Not a druid; an undead warluck who notices everything and lets stolen luck rot on the thief over time.

statetendencies.label: Attribute and Play Tendencies
statetendencies.summary: High Perception and Intelligence, with Luck treated as a conceptual or mechanical stat that swings with the moon.

tendencies.name: Observation Bias
tendencies.description: Invests heavily in perception and investigation to spot anomalies, patterns, and threats before committing to action.

tendencies.name: Analytic Mind
tendencies.description: Favors intelligence and reasoning to interpret signs and evidence, using DARAD-style cycles to avoid story-over-fact collapse.

tendencies.name: Fate-Weighted
tendencies.description: Luck (however modeled) is central: crit chances, rerolls, or narrative fortune events are more volatile but net favorable over time.

lunarLuckFrame.label: Lunar Luck Modulation Frame
lunarLuckFrame.summary: Defines how the warluck’s effective fortune and curse profile shifts across moon phases.

moonphases.name: New Moon
moonphases.luckvector: outward luck appears low, but curse reflection and misfortune DoT on enemies are strongest.
moonphases.playemphasis: revenge, hidden protection, turning hostile actions into long-term bad luck for the aggressor.

moonphases.name: Waxing Moon
moonphases.luckvector: personal risk-taking becomes more profitable; success odds on proactive plays quietly rise.
moonphases.playemphasis: initiating plans, gambles, and investigations that rely on incremental good breaks.

moonphases.name: Full Moon
moonphases.luckvector: peak warluck: both personal fortune and curse reflection spike.
moonphases.playemphasis: high-impact scenes where improbable successes and brutal backfires on enemies are most visible.

moonphases.name: Waning Moon
moonphases.luckvector: focus shifts to stripping and draining others’ luck, slowing or stopping their momentum.
moonphases.playemphasis: shutting down enemy streaks, unraveling deals, sabotaging long-term plans.

operationalrules: Treat moon phase as a narrative dial that changes which aspect of the warluck’s fortune is foregrounded.
The GM or system may bind these phases to real-world moons or an in-fiction lunar cycle.
At any phase, attempts to steal luck are valid triggers for misfortune effects; the phase only changes flavor and intensity.

curseFrame.label: Stolen Luck Misfortune DoT
curseFrame.summary: Soft, narrative-oriented damage-over-time style curse that attaches to anyone who attempts to steal or suppress the warluck’s fortune.

trigger.description: Another actor uses a power, spell, item, pact, exploit, or deal aimed at draining, copying, suppressing, or redirecting the warluck’s luck/fate/probability.
trigger.notes: Normal hostile actions do not trigger this; it is specific to tampering with luck or fate.

effectModel.baserule: Each tick, something goes meaningfully wrong for the cursed actor: failed checks at key moments, lost resources, spoiled opportunities, or narrative setbacks.
escalation: Early: small frustrations and low-impact failures.
Mid: disadvantage-like patterns, missed openings, broken tools, social blunders.
Late: major plan failures, ally loss, deal collapse, or other narrative-level hits.
removal: Voluntarily ceasing attempts to interfere with the warluck’s luck.
Making reparative action (breaking the exploit/pact, returning stolen gains, explicit amends).
Undergoing a strong ‘remove-curse’ style intervention if the setting supports it.

curseFrame.governingrule: The warluck does not actively cast this curse in most cases; reality corrects against sustained theft of their luck, with the undead warluck acting as the anchor point.
curseFrame.onelinetranslation: The longer someone tries to steal an undead warluck’s luck, the worse their own fate bleeds out in slow, accumulating misfortune.

undeadFlavorFrame.label: Undead Fortune Anchor Flavor
undeadFlavorFrame.summary: Describes how undeath changes the meaning of luck and consequence for the warluck.

elements.description: Having already died, the warluck’s relationship to risk is skewed: fortune tends to settle around them as a fixed reference instead of pushing them out of the world.
Misfortune manifestations have necrotic or graveyard tone: rusting gear, dead moments in conversations, opportunities decaying at the touch of those who tamper with the warluck’s fate.
Defense is more metaphysical than physical: they survive by making it increasingly costly for reality to allow other people’s theft of their luck.

reasoningAlignmentFrame.label: DARAD-Compatible Perception and Luck Use
reasoningAlignmentFrame.summary: Aligns the warluck’s decision-making with DARAD so they feel like an investigative realist, not a whimsical chaos mage.
alignmentpoints: Use DARAD Deduction 1 to lock what is actually observed before spending luck on big moves.
Generate multiple explanations (Abduction 1) for why luck is swinging, rather than assuming a single cause.
Use Reduction to strip narrative superstition from what the luck events actually prove.
Rebuild best explanations (Abduction 2) about who is under curse, why, and what the moon phase is emphasizing.
Use Deduction 2 to test predictions about future luck shifts before committing to major gambles.
reasoningAlignmentFrame.tagline: A warluck does not just feel lucky; they investigate what their luck is telling them.
